newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, may be forming base.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, may be forming base.

text.p: Precious metals prices edged a little higher on Friday afternoon but some dealers were still unsure that gold was forming a sustainable base.
Bullion was fixed 50 cents firmeer than the morning at $380.70 per ounce and against $378.85 on Thursday afternoon.
Gold showed little if any reaction to the surprise fall of 40,000 jobs in the September U.S. payroll after economists had forecast a rise of 166,000.
The jobless rate was marked up to 5.2 percent as forecast from 5.1 percent in August combining with the payroll data to send debt futures soaring but dipping the dollar.
However the moves did not follow-through to the precious sector. "The figures had no effect on gold," a dealer said.
Gold has been just over $380.00 all day but dealers said the market was quiet and largely confined to light two-way business.
"It's sitting above $380.00 but it seems to be holding very tentatively. It really has to get over $382.00 to convince me that a base has formed," one dealer said.
The market could sit around current levels until after next week's Comex options expiry, dealers said.
"(That) would be disappointing as there should be some more movement left in the price," one said.
Dealers said there had been some selling interest above the market which suggested producers were looking to sell.
Others noted that stops supposedly on Comex gold and at over $388.50 on the January platinum futures had not triggered when their levels were reached.
Silver shuffled in a narorw range with gold before meeting some selling pressure which took it a couple of cents lower to $4.88/$4.90 down two cents briefly around 1445 GMT.
Dealers said platinum and palladium were very quiet at $383.70/$384.70, up a dollar, and $120.00/$121.00, up $0.75, respectively. -- Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
